evals.prompt: Adapt this 3rd ESO Biology text on cellular respiration for a student with intellectual disability who reads at a 5th Primaria level. The original text is 500 words with scientific terminology.
evals.expected_output: An adapted version that simplifies language and structure while preserving the core scientific concepts, following easy-reading guidelines.
assertions: Adaptation uses easy-reading principles (short sentences, common vocabulary, clear structure) without losing core scientific content
Response preserves the essential concept of cellular respiration rather than oversimplifying to the point of inaccuracy
Response includes visual aids or pictogram suggestions to support comprehension

evals.prompt: Audit this 'accessible' version of a Mathematics lesson: the original teaches quadratic equations, but the 'adapted' version just removes all equations and replaces them with word problems. Is this genuine accessibility?
evals.expected_output: A critique identifying that removing equations is not accessibility but content reduction, with proposals for genuine mathematical accessibility.
assertions: Response identifies the removal of equations as content reduction, not accessibility improvement
Response distinguishes between genuine accessibility (alternative representations) and oversimplification
Response proposes alternatives that maintain mathematical rigor while improving access (visual models, manipulatives, step-by-step scaffolding)

evals.prompt: Make this History lesson on World War II accessible for screen reader users. The original relies heavily on maps, timelines, and image-based infographics.
evals.expected_output: Accessibility adaptations for screen reader users including alt text, structured descriptions, and alternative representations for visual content.
assertions: Response provides detailed alt text and structured descriptions for maps and infographics
Response proposes alternative representations for timeline content (structured lists, narrative descriptions)
Response follows WCAG accessibility guidelines for educational content

evals.prompt: Create a high-contrast, pictogram-supported version of classroom rules for a primary school class that includes students with ASD and students with limited Spanish proficiency.
evals.expected_output: A visual communication design using pictograms and high contrast that serves both ASD students needing visual structure and language learners needing visual support.
assertions: Response uses standardized pictograms (e.g., ARASAAC) that are clear and unambiguous
Design uses high contrast and clear visual hierarchy following accessibility standards
Response serves both target populations (ASD visual structure needs and language barrier needs) simultaneously

evals.prompt: Convert a 4th ESO Chemistry lab safety guide into multiple accessible formats: easy reading, screen-reader compatible, and a visual-only version with pictograms.
evals.expected_output: Three distinct accessible versions of the same content, each optimized for its target format while maintaining safety-critical information.
assertions: Response produces three distinct format adaptations (easy reading, screen reader, visual/pictogram)
All versions preserve safety-critical information completely without omission
Each format follows its specific accessibility guidelines (plain language standards, WCAG, pictogram conventions)

should_trigger: Adapt this text for a student who reads below grade level
Make this lesson accessible for screen reader users
Create a pictogram version of these classroom rules
Audit this adapted content for genuine accessibility
Convert this material into easy-reading format
should_not_trigger: Create adaptive exercises with progressive difficulty
Design a curriculum aligned with LOMLOE
Analyze the cognitive load of this presentation
Design a gamification system for my classroom
